title: Subset probability equals its layer weight
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $S$ be a subset of an $n$-element set. Under the distribution obtained by choosing a size uniformly from $0,1,\ldots,n$ and then choosing uniformly among subsets of that size, the probability of selecting $S$, viewed as a real number, equals its Shapley layer weight, namely $1/((n+1)\binom{n}{|S|})$.
hypotheses_covered: $S$ is a subset of an $n$-element set
